answers.rationale: Inline diffs are crucial for me to maintain control. I'd definitely use this feature if I can see exactly what changes are being made before accepting them. That review step is what makes autonomous editing feel safe.

Checkpoint rollback is a game-changer for me. Knowing I can instantly revert to a previous state if something goes wrong makes me way more willing to let an agent work autonomously on complex tasks. It removes the fear of irreversible mistakes.

My biggest worry is that the agent might introduce subtle bugs or logic errors that pass initial review but break functionality downstream. Even with diffs, catching all incorrect changes is hard, especially in complex codebases.

answers.value: Refactoring variable names or adding type annotations in a well-tested module with good test coverage
answers.rationale: I'd start with low-risk mechanical changes that don't alter logic. Refactoring names or adding types are easy to review, unlikely to introduce bugs, and have clear success criteria. Tests would catch any issues immediately.
